To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the optimal diversity performance of space-time block code transmission over distributed MIMO Rayleigh channels is achieved by implementing transmit power allocation at the receiver based only on transmit and receive correlation information.

the optimal diversity performance of STBCs in distributed MIMO channels is achieved by transmit power allocation implemented in the receiver based on the knowledge of transmit and receive correlation matrices.

optimal power allocation can significantly improve SER performance of STBCs in correlated D-MIMO Rayleigh fading channels, and that the optimal diversity performance is affected by large-scale fading, targeted data-rate, antenna correlations and power.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the optimal performance of STBCs over D-MIMO channels, with the main contributions being the derivation of optimal power allocation schemes for open loop STBC transmissions, and a close analogy between STBCs in open loop co-located MIMOs and D-MIMO systems.

the optimal diversity performance of STBCs in correlated D-MIMO Rayleigh fading channels, and the proposed schemes can significantly improve the performance of STBC-based wireless systems over correlated D-MIMOs, especially for those systems with limited feedback.

optimal transmission of STBCs over correlated D-MIMOs with the goal to maximize the diversity performance, which is achieved by optimal power allocation at the receiver based upon channel state information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the optimal diversity performance of STBCs in a D-MIMO system can be achieved with the proposed optimal power allocation scheme, and the performance of the proposed sub-optimal schemes is very close to optimal.
the optimal diversity performance is not necessarily achieved through the optimal number of DAs, but through transmit power optimization.

the optimal SER of open loop STBC transmission is achieved through optimal power allocation implemented at receiver, and the optimal performance of open loop STB transmission over correlated D-Mimo channels approaches optimal performance of co-located MIMOs with minimum feedback.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the optimal SER of uncoded STBMs over a generalized DA topology can be achieved through transmit power control at the receiver, with the optimal power allocation being determined based on the channel state information of the transmit antennas, the receive antennas, and the large scale fading.
, the optimal diversity performance of STBCs in distributed MIMO channels can be achieved by transmit power allocation based on transmit and receiver correlations.
optimal STBCs over correlated D-MIMOs can be efficiently designed and implemented, which can significantly reduce feedback overhead, while achieving optimal diversity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimal diversity of STBCs in correlated D-MIMO can be achieved through power allocation, with a close analogy to co-located MISO systems.

the optimal diversity performance of STBCs in distributed MIMO can approach that of co-located MIMOs with the help of optimal transmit power allocation, which can be implemented by a receiver without requiring any feedback from the transmitter.

optimal power allocation is essential to achieve full diversity in correlated D-MIMO STBCs, and that the optimal diversity performance is highly sensitive to the large scale fading, antenna correlations and targeted data rate.
